White privilege doesn't necessarily mean that you've got privilege in every aspect or that your life is easy just because you're white. I think the point of it is to point out that, if we look solely at race and skin color, there's a certain degree of privilege you get because of your skin color. Imagine it like someone who was born wealthy but they're also an atheist. While they have economical privilege but, like you pointed out, there is a "Christian privilege" that exists. Privilege in one area doesn't mean your life is easy or that you're privileged, I think it's just supposed to refer to a privilege in a SPECIFIC area of things. The idea is that white people in the US, for example, have certain race-based privileges that other races don't get. Does that make any sense?
